text: CS301 - Operating Systems Course Handout / Syllabus Unit 1: Introduction to Operating Systems - What is an operating system, goals and functions - Types of operating systems: batch, multiprogrammed, time-sharing, distributed, real-time - System calls and system programs overview Unit 2: Process Management - Process concept, process states, process control block - Process scheduling queues and schedulers - CPU scheduling: First Come First Serve (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Round Robin - Brief comparison of scheduling algorithms using turnaround time and waiting time Unit 3: Process Synchronization - Critical section problem, Peterson's solution - Semaphores: definition and usage (introductory treatment only, one lecture) - Classical synchronization problems mentioned by name only: producer-consumer, readers-writers Unit 4: Memory Management - Contiguous

section problem, Peterson's solution - Semaphores: definition and usage (introductory treatment only, one lecture) - Classical synchronization problems mentioned by name only: producer-consumer, readers-writers Unit 4: Memory Management - Contiguous memory allocation, fragmentation - Paging: basic concept, page tables - Segmentation: basic concept - Virtual memory overview, demand paging Unit 5: File Systems and Storage - File concepts, directory structure - File allocation methods: contiguous, linked, indexed - Disk structure overview Unit 6: Miscellaneous Topics - Deadlocks: definition and the four necessary conditions (single slide, not covered in depth) - Protection and security: brief overview Note: Disk scheduling algorithms (SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK) and deadlock avoidance algorithms (Banker's Algorithm) are NOT covered in lecture slides this semester due to time constraints;
